title: Deterministic event ordering and lossless retry layer for user-visibility metrics
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Problem: Some downstream consumers (billing, per-tenant dashboards, alerting) require deterministic ordering of user-visible metric events and a lossless retry semantics during transient failure windows. Current best-effort ingest can reorder events under shard rebalances and produce duplicates after retries, causing spikes in per-tenant counters and noisy alerts.

Goal: Implement a streaming layer component that provides: deterministic per-tenant ordering (by logical sequence), at-least-once delivery with duplicate suppression, bounded retry backoff to avoid hot replays, and low operational overhead. This cannot add large end-to-end latency for common paths.

Non-functional constraints:
- Maintain 95th token latency budget for metric commits (target +20ms overhead).
- Support 10k concurrent tenant shards with modest memory footprint.
- Avoid global coordination for normal-path ordering; prefer per-shard leases.
- Provide instrumentation: per-tenant reorder/duplicate rate metrics, commit lag, retry queue depth.

Scope:
1) Producer-side: augment metric envelope with monotonic tenant_seq and opaque retry_token when retried. Provide SDK helpers for idempotent emissions.
2) Broker/shard: keep minimal sequencing watermark per-tenant and persist small ring buffer of recent seq IDs for dedupe. Use append-only topic with per-tenant keying to keep natural partition affinity.
3) Stream processor: deterministic reorder window using tenant_seq and a configurable late-arrival tolerance; emit a resolution marker when gaps are closed or timed out.
4) Retry layer: bounded, backoff-aware replay queue with randomized jitter and circuit-breaker to prevent thundering replays on recoveries.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Strong ordering via single-tenant partitions vs. per-tenant logical sequence with cross-partition reconciliation. We chose per-tenant logical sequencing with partition affinity to reduce hot-spot risk and allow rebalancing without global pause.
- Synchronous durable seq persistence vs. in-memory watermark with checkpointing. We use a small durable watermark checkpoint (RocksDB-backed state store) to survive worker restarts while keeping common-path fast.

High-level design links: Confluence design: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/REORDER-119876, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metrics-pipeline/pull/246, performance dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/metrics/reordering-prototype
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant events are emitted downstream in tenant_seq order for >99.9% of cases within configured reorder window
Duplicate events suppressed by dedupe layer; downstream duplicate rate reduced by >=95% compared to baseline
End-to-end median/95th latency impact of new layer < +20ms / +50ms respectively under typical load
System tolerates single-worker crash and recovers without creating sustained duplicate floods
Instrumentation added: reorder_rate, duplicate_rate, retry_queue_depth, per-tenant lag percentiles, and SLO dashboards
notes: Prototype implemented a RocksDB state store per worker for tenant watermarks; initial memory footprint ~4KB/tenant active window
Benchmark: 200k events/s sustained across 40 workers with median extra CPU ~8% and p95 latency +12ms
We observed pathological tenants with bursty writes — added token-bucket downsampling and suggested per-tenant rate limits in configs

Edge-case: clock skew between producers may produce non-monotonic tenant_seq if producers are multi-writer; SDK will emit a monotonic local sequence and server-side will accept out-of-order if within tolerance
implementation_plan: Week 1: SDK changes for tenant_seq and retry_token + unit tests
Week 2: Shard worker watermark persistence and dedupe cache implementation
Week 3: Stream processor reorder-window logic, integration tests with staging cluster
Week 4: Canary rollout to 10% of tenants + monitor regressions, iterate on backoff parameters
Week 5: Full rollout and postmortem/observability cleanup
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large number of active tenants causes state bloat — Mitigation: LRU eviction + checkpoint compaction and tiered storage for inactive tenants
Risk: Retry storms after partition recovery — Mitigation: randomized jitter, exponential backoff, and circuit-breaker per-tenant
Risk: Increased latency for cold-starting tenants — Mitigation: fast-path bypass for new tenants until watermark established, with higher tolerance for duplicates transiently

2026-03-05 Evan Morales (review): Prefer RocksDB for durability. Suggest exposing reorder_window as a tenant-configurable flag; added review comment on canary gating metrics.
2026-03-08 Diego Alvarez: Integrated dedupe cache with TTL 10m, fallback to tombstone marker on out-of-window duplicates. Staging tests show duplicate rate down 97%.
2026-03-12 SRE Rotation: Load test uncovered a tenant causing hotspot during recovery. We added token-bucket throttle and will test again with 10x load generator.
2026-03-13 Priya Rao: Design doc accepted. Next deliverable: canary rollout plan and playbook for fast rollbacks.
